findings.title: Mobile app resets notification preferences to all-on after every app update
findings.description: Members who deliberately opt out of push notifications (session reminders, nudges, goal-tracking pings) in the mobile app have their preferences wiped back to default (all-on) every time the app updates, silently re-subscribing them. Confirmed on both iOS and Android, occurring across at least three separate app updates. Only in-app push notification settings are affected; web preferences and email settings are unaffected. Customer reports 11 complaints within two days following one such update, with opted-out machinists now threatening to delete the app.
findings.quote: every time the mobile app updates, those settings get wiped. The notification preferences reset back to the defaults, which is everything ON.
findings.severity_reason: Silently overrides an explicit user privacy/attention preference on every release across both platforms, and the customer states it is actively jeopardizing adoption/retention on a floor rollout (a deliberate opt-out being un-done is effectively an unresolved defect with no confirmed workaround yet).
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue covers notification-preference persistence across app updates; distinct from PROJ-110 (Android launch crash) and PROJ-160 (iOS logout after OS update), which are different symptoms/scopes.

findings.title: N/A - customer-built onboarding process, not a BetterBark product topic
findings.description: Devon and Renata describe a QR code posted at the time clock that lets machinists scan in and register for BetterBark, which drove strong floor adoption. This is a customer-side onboarding tactic using an existing app entry point, not a request to change or fix any BetterBark product capability.
findings.quote: They showed up because we made it dead simple. One QR code by the time clock, scan, you're in. No friction.
findings.severity_reason: No defect or feature gap in the product; purely a customer rollout tactic shared for context.
findings.match_note: Not a BetterBark product defect or feature request; it's the customer's own onboarding process built around the existing app, mentioned as positive context before the actual escalation.
